title: Coast to coast on foot
paragraphs: In 2015, a retired teacher called Tom Hale set {off} from New York with nothing {but} a backpack and a pair of comfortable boots. His plan was to walk all the way to San Francisco, a journey {of} more than 4,000 kilometres. Hardly {anyone} believed he would make it.

The first weeks were the hardest. Tom had never walked {such} long distances before, and his feet were soon covered {in} blisters. But he grew stronger, and strangers began to recognise him thanks {to} the photos he posted online. One family in Kansas even invited him to stay {for} a whole week.

Tom finally reached San Francisco eight months later, {having} raised over $50,000 for a children's hospital. When journalists asked him about the hardest part, he said it was not the walking {itself} but the loneliness. 'I have never felt as tired, or as happy, {as} I did on that last day,' he said. He is now planning to walk across Australia, although his wife says he will have to do it {without} her.

gaps.label: set off / set out
gaps.explanation: SET OFF y SET OUT = salir, emprender un viaje.

gaps.label: nothing but
gaps.explanation: NOTHING BUT = nada más que. EXCEPT también sirve: nada excepto.

gaps.label: a journey of + distancia
gaps.explanation: Con una medida, el sustantivo lleva OF: 'a journey of 4,000 km', 'a delay of two hours'.

gaps.label: hardly anyone
gaps.explanation: HARDLY ya es negativo, así que va con ANYONE/ANYBODY, no con NOBODY ni SOMEBODY.

gaps.label: such + adjetivo + sustantivo
gaps.explanation: SUCH va delante de adjetivo + sustantivo: 'such long distances'. SO va solo con el adjetivo: 'so long'.

gaps.label: covered in / with
gaps.explanation: 'covered IN' o 'covered WITH' = cubierto de. Las dos son correctas.

gaps.label: thanks to
gaps.explanation: THANKS TO + sustantivo = gracias a. Es fija.

gaps.label: for + período
gaps.explanation: FOR + un período de tiempo: 'stay for a week'.

gaps.label: having + participio
gaps.explanation: HAVING + participio expresa una acción anterior a la principal: primero juntó el dinero, después llegó.

gaps.label: pronombre enfático
gaps.explanation: ITSELF enfatiza el sustantivo: 'not the walking itself' = no la caminata en sí.

gaps.label: as … as
gaps.explanation: La comparación de igualdad es AS + adjetivo + AS. La frase ya tiene el primer AS: 'as happy as'.

gaps.label: without
gaps.explanation: WITHOUT = sin. El 'although' anuncia que la esposa no piensa acompañarlo.

title: Can you learn while you sleep?
paragraphs: Wouldn't it be wonderful {if} you could learn a new language while you slept? For years, companies have sold recordings {that} claim to do exactly this. Unfortunately, there is very {little} evidence that they work. Most studies have found that the brain is simply not able {to} store new words during deep sleep.

However, a recent experiment suggests that sleep can still play an important role. Volunteers studied a list of Dutch words in the evening and then went to bed. Half {of} them heard the words again, very quietly, {during} the night. The next morning, this group remembered far more words {than} the others.

The researchers stress, {however}, that the volunteers had already learnt the words {before} going to sleep. In {other} words, sleep can help you to remember, but it cannot do the learning {for} you. So if you are hoping to become fluent in Spanish without opening a book, you will be disappointed, {no} matter how many recordings you buy.

gaps.label: if (condicional)
gaps.explanation: IF introduce la condición imaginaria: 'it would be wonderful if you could…'.

gaps.label: relativo that / which
gaps.explanation: Relativo para cosas en una oración especificativa: THAT o WHICH.

gaps.label: little + incontable
gaps.explanation: EVIDENCE es incontable: va con LITTLE. 'Very little evidence' = casi ninguna prueba.

gaps.label: be able to
gaps.explanation: BE ABLE TO + infinitivo = ser capaz de.

gaps.label: half of them
gaps.explanation: Delante de un pronombre, HALF necesita OF: 'half of them', nunca 'half them'.

gaps.label: during the night
gaps.explanation: DURING, IN o THROUGH THE NIGHT: en algún momento, o a lo largo, de la noche.

gaps.label: more … than
gaps.explanation: Después de un comparativo ('far more words') viene THAN.

gaps.label: however entre comas
gaps.explanation: HOWEVER (o THOUGH) entre comas marca el contraste con lo anterior.

gaps.label: before + -ing
gaps.explanation: BEFORE + -ing = antes de hacer algo. El 'already' confirma que el aprendizaje fue previo.

gaps.label: in other words
gaps.explanation: IN OTHER WORDS = dicho de otro modo. Es fija.

gaps.label: do something for someone
gaps.explanation: 'do the learning FOR you' = hacerlo en tu lugar.

gaps.label: no matter how
gaps.explanation: NO MATTER HOW/WHAT = no importa cuánto/qué. Es fija.

title: The café with no prices
paragraphs: When Ana Ruiz opened her café in Valencia three years {ago}, she made a decision that surprised everyone: there would be no prices on the menu. Customers would simply pay {whatever} they thought the food was worth. Her friends warned her that people would take advantage {of} her generosity and that she would be out of business {within} a year.

The opposite turned out to be true. Most customers pay more than the usual price, and some leave {as} much as double. Ana believes this is {because} people appreciate being trusted. 'When you treat people {like} adults, they behave like adults,' she explains. Of course, there are a {few} customers who pay almost nothing, but Ana does not mind.

The café has become {so} popular that there is often a queue outside the door. Several other restaurants in the city have tried the same idea, {although} not all of them have been as successful. Ana thinks that the secret is not the prices {but} the atmosphere. 'People come back because they feel at home here, not because they can eat {for} free.'

gaps.label: tiempo + ago
gaps.explanation: AGO va DESPUÉS del período y con pasado simple: 'three years ago'.

gaps.label: whatever / what
gaps.explanation: WHATEVER (o WHAT) = lo que sea que. Introduce la cantidad que cada cliente decide.

gaps.label: take advantage of
gaps.explanation: TAKE ADVANTAGE OF = aprovecharse de. Es fija.

gaps.label: within a year
gaps.explanation: WITHIN o IN + período = antes de que pase ese tiempo.

gaps.label: as much as
gaps.explanation: AS MUCH AS + cantidad remarca que es mucho: 'as much as double'.

gaps.label: this is because
gaps.explanation: 'This is because' + oración explica la causa de lo anterior.

gaps.label: treat someone like / as
gaps.explanation: 'treat someone LIKE / AS an adult' = tratar a alguien como a un adulto.

gaps.label: a few + contable
gaps.explanation: CUSTOMERS es contable plural: 'a few customers' = algunos clientes.

gaps.label: so … that
gaps.explanation: SO + adjetivo + THAT = tan… que. Con sustantivo sería SUCH.

gaps.label: although + frase reducida
gaps.explanation: ALTHOUGH / THOUGH introduce un contraste: probaron la idea, pero no a todos les fue bien.

gaps.label: not … but
gaps.explanation: NOT X BUT Y = no X sino Y.

gaps.label: for free
gaps.explanation: FOR FREE = gratis. Es fija.

title: The day the internet stopped
paragraphs: Last Tuesday, the internet in our town went down {for} almost twelve hours. At first, nobody knew {what} to do. My brother spent the first hour restarting the router again and again, {as} if that would make any difference, while my parents kept checking their phones {in} case the connection had come back.

By lunchtime, {however}, something strange had started to happen. People who had lived next door to each {other} for years started talking in the street. My mother discovered that our neighbour, {whose} garden she had admired for years, was a retired botanist. Children who normally spent their afternoons in front of a screen were playing football in the park {instead}.

When the connection was restored that evening, most people went back {to} their screens immediately. But not everyone. Our street has decided to hold a party once {a} month, with or without the internet. It took a broken cable to remind us {how} much we were missing.

gaps.label: for + período
gaps.explanation: FOR + duración: 'for almost twelve hours'.

gaps.label: know what to do
gaps.explanation: 'know WHAT to do' = saber qué hacer. Es pronombre interrogativo + infinitivo.

gaps.label: as if
gaps.explanation: AS IF = como si. Describe algo que no es real: reiniciar el router no cambiaba nada.

gaps.label: in case
gaps.explanation: IN CASE = por si acaso. Es fija.

gaps.label: however entre comas
gaps.explanation: HOWEVER (o THOUGH) entre comas marca el contraste con lo anterior.

gaps.label: each other
gaps.explanation: EACH OTHER = el uno al otro.

gaps.label: whose (posesivo)
gaps.explanation: WHOSE = cuyo. El jardín es DEL vecino.

gaps.label: instead (al final)
gaps.explanation: INSTEAD al final de la oración = en cambio, en lugar de eso.

gaps.label: go back to
gaps.explanation: GO BACK TO something = volver a algo.

gaps.label: once a month
gaps.explanation: Para frecuencias: 'once A month' o 'once EVERY month'.

gaps.label: how much
gaps.explanation: HOW MUCH = cuánto. Introduce una exclamación indirecta.

title: A year abroad
paragraphs: Every year, thousands {of} students decide to spend a year studying in another country. For many of them, it is the first time they have lived away {from} home. Living abroad is not always easy. Students have to get used {to} a different culture, and many of them find it hard to make friends {at} first.

However, most students agree that the benefits are greater {than} the difficulties they face at the start. Not {only} do they improve their language skills, but they also become more independent. They learn to solve problems {by} themselves and to look after their own money.

Many students say that the experience changed the {way} they see the world. Some even decide to stay {in} the country after they finish their studies. Employers also value international experience, {which} is why students who have studied abroad often find work more quickly. So if you ever {have} the chance, don't think twice!

gaps.label: thousands of
gaps.explanation: THOUSANDS / HUNDREDS / MILLIONS llevan OF delante del sustantivo.

gaps.label: away from
gaps.explanation: AWAY FROM = lejos de: 'away from home'.

gaps.label: get used to
gaps.explanation: GET USED TO + sustantivo o -ing = acostumbrarse a.

gaps.label: at first
gaps.explanation: AT FIRST = al principio.

gaps.label: greater than
gaps.explanation: Después del comparativo 'greater' viene THAN.

gaps.label: not only … but also
gaps.explanation: NOT ONLY + inversión (do they improve) … BUT ALSO.

gaps.label: by / for themselves
gaps.explanation: BY THEMSELVES = solos, sin ayuda. FOR THEMSELVES = por su cuenta. Las dos valen acá.

gaps.label: the way + oración
gaps.explanation: 'the WAY they see the world' = la forma en que ven el mundo.

gaps.label: stay in a country
gaps.explanation: Con países y ciudades: 'stay IN the country'.

gaps.label: which is why
gaps.explanation: ', WHICH is why' retoma toda la oración anterior. THAT no puede ir después de coma.

gaps.label: have / get the chance
gaps.explanation: 'have the chance' o 'get the chance' = tener la oportunidad.

title: Borrow a drill, not a book
paragraphs: Why buy a drill {that} you will only use twice a year? This is the question behind 'libraries of things', {where} people borrow tools instead of books. Members pay a small fee and can borrow anything {from} a sewing machine to a tent.

The idea is simple, but it has {been} remarkably successful. The first library of this kind in our city now has more than 600 members, and it is run entirely {by} volunteers. Its founder, Kate Morris, came up {with} the idea after moving into a small flat. 'I had no space for things I rarely used, and I realised I couldn't {be} the only one,' she says.

Supporters say these libraries are good not just for people's wallets {but} also for the planet. Every item that is shared means one {less} product needs to be made. Some members also say that the library has helped them get to know their neighbours, {something} they had never managed before. Kate hopes that, one day, there will be a library {like} this in every town.

gaps.label: relativo that / which
gaps.explanation: Relativo para cosas: THAT o WHICH.

gaps.label: where (relativo de lugar)
gaps.explanation: WHERE = donde. Introduce lo que pasa en esas bibliotecas.

gaps.label: from … to
gaps.explanation: 'anything FROM X TO Y' = cualquier cosa, desde X hasta Y.

gaps.label: has been + adjetivo
gaps.explanation: Present perfect de BE: 'has BEEN successful'. 'Has proved / proven successful' también es correcto.

gaps.label: pasiva + by
gaps.explanation: En pasiva, quien hace la acción va con BY: 'run by volunteers'.

gaps.label: come up with
gaps.explanation: COME UP WITH = ocurrírsele algo.

gaps.label: modal + be
gaps.explanation: Después de un modal va el infinitivo sin TO: 'couldn't BE'.

gaps.label: not just … but also
gaps.explanation: NOT JUST / NOT ONLY … BUT ALSO.

gaps.label: one less / one fewer
gaps.explanation: 'one LESS product' es lo más común; 'one FEWER' es la forma más formal.

gaps.label: aposición con something
gaps.explanation: ', SOMETHING they had never managed' resume lo anterior. ', WHICH they had never managed' también vale.

gaps.label: like this
gaps.explanation: LIKE THIS = como esta. SUCH no puede ir en esa posición.
